scope: Corollary 4.6 (Upper bound for convex loss perturbations) of the manuscript “Microscopic jamming in the negative spherical perceptron” (preprints/Microscopic-jamming-in-the-negative-spherical-perceptron-September-24-2026/Microscopic-jamming-in-the-negative-spherical-perceptron-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 222 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8d94e973e689e60b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ψ ∈ C∞ c ((−∞, 0)). There is w0 > 0, independent of β, such that for both signs of w with |w| < w0 the loss Lw(z) = V (z) + wψ(1 + z) is nonnegative, convex, and nonincreasing. For every fixed β > 0 and every fixed profile q with q∗ < 1, lim sup N→∞ PN (−βLw) ≤ αΦ−βLw (q) + E(q). (4.12) More generally this upper bound holds for any nonpositive, concave, nondecreasing terminal of at most quadratic growth which agrees with a negative quadratic hinge outside a compact set.
